detections.name: WISE 0855−0714
detections.note: Too faint for the automatic search to find in single images. Measuring exactly where the catalogue says it should be gives 0.526 mJy on average over 7 frames, 4.4 times the spread of the same measurement at 383 random spots in this field. 6% of those random spots are at least as bright. It should only shift 1.3 pixels across these frames, so the images alone cannot show that this faint smudge is the moving brown dwarf.

notes: The coordinates in the challenge (08h55m10.831s −07d14m42.53s) are where WISE saw it in 2010. It moves 8.1″ a year to the west, so by 2026 it is about 2′ away from that spot.
The crosshair shows where the star catalogue says the object should be on each date, given its motion of 8.2″ a year. Across these frames that is a shift of 1.3 pixels (8.0″).
